intro.title: PropTypes / TypeScript Interface
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Angular component that displays user profile information, such as a name and age. You will learn how to define and use a TypeScript interface to strictly type the data your component receives, ensuring it matches the expected structure. This involves creating an interface, applying it to a component's input property, and using the typed data in your template. By the end, you'll understand how interfaces help catch errors early and make your Angular code more reliable and maintainable.
intro.usecase: TypeScript interfaces are essential for building maintainable enterprise applications like customer dashboards and admin panels. In a dashboard component, interfaces define the structure of data objects like user profiles, sales metrics, or inventory items, ensuring type safety across complex data flows. When creating reusable form components or data tables, interfaces specify the expected props for inputs, validation rules, and event handlers. This prevents runtime errors in production applications and enables better IDE support during development of features like dynamic filters or interactive charts.
